record.original_question: Let St be a Steiner tree in Euclidean space, let A be its terminal set, and fix x and r > 0 so that Br(x) contains no terminal points, that is, A ∩ Br(x) = ∅. Assume moreover that the tree has finite length inside Br(x). A branching point of a Steiner tree is a non-terminal vertex of degree 3. For t = 1/2, or more generally for t ∈ (0, 1), what is the largest possible number of branching points of St that can lie inside Btr(x)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be a finite (or closed) set, called the set of terminals, and let $\mathrm{St} \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be a Steiner tree on $A$, i.e. a connected set containing $A$ that (locally) minimizes one-dimensional Hausdorff measure $\mathcal{H}^1$ among connected sets containing $A$. Assume $\mathrm{St}$ has finite length. Then $\mathrm{St}$ is compact, contains no loops, and the edges of $\mathrm{St}\setminus A$ are straight line segments; every vertex has degree at most $3$; only terminals may have degree $1$ or $2$; every non-terminal vertex has degree exactly $3$ and is called a branching (Steiner) point. At every branching point the three incident edges meet pairwise at angles of $2\pi/3$ (so a neighborhood of a branching point is a planar regular tripod).

Fix a point $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$ and a radius $r > 0$, and let $B_r(x)$ denote the open Euclidean ball of radius $r$ centered at $x$. Suppose
$$A \cap B_r(x) = \varnothing \qquad \text{and} \qquad \mathcal{H}^1(\mathrm{St} \cap B_r(x)) < \infty.$$

For a parameter $t \in (0,1)$ (in particular for $t = 1/2$), determine the largest possible cardinality
$$N(t,d) \;=\; \sup \big\{\, \#\{\text{branching points of } \mathrm{St} \text{ in } B_{tr}(x)\} \,\big\},$$
where the supremum is taken over all Steiner trees $\mathrm{St} \subset \mathbb{R}^d$, all terminal sets $A$, and all balls $B_r(x)$ satisfying the conditions above.
artifact.status_search_result: The question appears in a recent collection of open problems on Steiner trees and maximal distance minimizers (Teplitskaya, 2025), where it is explicitly listed as an open question. No subsequent work resolving the density of branching points in $B_{tr}(x)$ for $t \in (0,1)$ was found.
